# Representation and Kernel Modifications


## Overview
This family of methods modifies the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation or the rendering kernel to improve geometric fidelity, storage efficiency, or modeling flexibility. While standard 3DGS uses positive, isotropic/anisotropic Gaussians with fixed exponential kernels, these variants introduce negative primitives, hierarchical scaffolding, geometric regularization, alternative radial basis functions, or grid-based blur kernels. They address specific limitations such as the inability to model complex nonlinear structures, noisy geometry, high storage costs, or the rigidity of the Gaussian kernel family.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the differentiable rendering framework of 3D Gaussian Splatting [Parent](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md). They share the core data structure of 3D Gaussians defined by position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$ (often represented via spherical harmonics). The rendering pipeline involves projecting these 3D primitives to 2D ellipses, sorting by depth, and accumulating color via alpha blending. The modifications occur either in the **primitive representation** (e.g., adding negative colors, anchoring to a grid, orienting normals) or in the **kernel function** (e.g., replacing the exponential Gaussian with other decaying functions or blur kernels). Optimization is performed via gradient descent to minimize reconstruction loss, often with additional regularization terms specific to the variant.

## Subtopics

### [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) extends 3DGS by incorporating "negative Gaussians"—ellipsoids with negative color values—into the scene representation. This allows the modeling of high-frequency elements, complex nonlinear structures, and rapid color transitions that standard positive Gaussians represent inefficiently. Unlike standard 3DGS, which requires many components to approximate complex shapes, NegGS uses the cancellation effect between positive and negative Gaussians to achieve greater flexibility with fewer total primitives. It is chosen when the scene contains complex, non-convex, or high-frequency details that are difficult to capture with positive-only primitives.

### [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)
[Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md) is a Gaussian-based scene representation that utilizes anchor points to establish a hierarchical and region-aware 3D scene structure. It predicts neural Gaussian attributes on-the-fly based on viewing direction and distance. Unlike vanilla 3D-GS, which allows Gaussians to freely drift and split, Scaffold-GS exploits scene structure to guide and constrain Gaussian distribution while allowing local adaptation to varying viewing angles. It achieves comparable or superior reconstruction quality with significantly reduced storage requirements (4.4x–10.2x reduction) and real-time rendering speeds. It is chosen when storage efficiency and hierarchical scene representation are prioritized.

### [GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)
[GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md) is a training optimization and initialization strategy that improves geometric consistency and surface reconstruction quality. It addresses the issue of noisy or inconsistent geometry in standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by densifying Gaussians on the tangent plane of existing Gaussians and encouraging smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring Gaussians. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like Negative Gaussian Splatting or Scaffold-GS by focusing specifically on local geometric regularization and tangent-space densification rather than negative primitives, scaffolding structures, or frequency-domain blur kernels. It is chosen when high-quality, smooth surface reconstruction is required.

### [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)
[DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md) is a method for differentiable volume rendering that replaces the standard Gaussian reconstruction kernels with a broader class of functions called Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs). It solves the limitation of being restricted to the exponential family by allowing non-exponential kernels (e.g., half-cosine, inverse multiquadric) that offer faster training convergence and lower memory usage while maintaining comparable visual quality. Unlike standard 3DGS, which relies on the closed-form integration properties of Gaussians, DARBF-Splatting introduces a correction factor to approximate this efficiency for other kernel types. It is chosen when faster convergence or specific kernel properties (like finite support) are desired.

### [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)
[Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md) replaces neural network-generated blur kernels with a learnable, indexed grid to model spatially-varying blurriness in differentiable rendering. Unlike methods that use Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) to predict kernel weights per pixel, this approach assigns pixels to discrete sharpness groups, allowing expressivity to scale with grid size without additional computational cost during inference. It is chosen when modeling defocus or blur effects efficiently is required.

### Gaussian Shell Maps
[Gaussian Shell Maps](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) combine CNN-based generators with 3DGS to recreate virtual humans with sophisticated details such as clothing and accessories.

### Gaussian Wrapping
[Gaussian Wrapping](9186-scaffold-gs.md) is a framework that reinterprets 3D Gaussian primitives as oriented probabilistic surface elements representing geometry only within an oriented half-space, allowing derivation of closed-form occupancy, vacancy, and normal fields for watertight mesh extraction. It models surface points with asymmetric primitives where the Gaussian models density decay on the outward-facing side, while the inward-facing side is considered fully occupied. It identifies geometric gaps where the oriented surface assumption is violated and densifies the representation to obtain a watertight shell of oriented primitives. It introduces a learnable oriented normal at each Gaussian element and defines an adapted attenuation formulation to enable closed-form expressions for normal and occupancy fields. It introduces a novel consistency loss and a dedicated densification strategy to enforce Gaussians to wrap the entire surface by closing geometric holes. It modifies the differentiable rasterizer to output depth as an isosurface of the continuous model. It uses Primal Adaptive Meshing for Region-of-Interest meshing at arbitrary resolution.

## Background
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 as a real-time rendering method for 3D scenes [Parent](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md). The variants in this family emerged to address specific limitations of the original method:
*   **Negative Gaussians** were introduced to handle complex shapes and high-frequency details more efficiently [S1, S2].
*   **Scaffold-GS** was developed to reduce storage costs and provide hierarchical scene representation [S2].
*   **GeoGaussian** was proposed to improve geometric smoothness and surface quality [S1].
*   **DARBF-Splatting** explored alternative kernel functions for faster convergence and memory efficiency [S1].
*   **Grid-based Blur Kernels** were introduced to model spatially-varying blur efficiently [S1].
*   **Gaussian Wrapping** was developed to enable watertight mesh extraction from Gaussian splats by treating them as oriented surface elements [S2].
*   **Gaussian Shell Maps** were used for animatable human reconstruction [S1].

These methods are used in various applications including static scene reconstruction, human avatar creation, surface reconstruction, and dynamic scene modeling.
